analysis:
Examined both CI source excerpts, documentation metadata and the complete supplied documentation patch against the indexed threat model and selected T-041 detail. .github/workflows/ci.yml:43-47 replaces one five-job provider lane with five one-job lanes; line 142 selects the matching route using the fixed shard matrix at lines 147-148. Conditions, runner profile, fallback labels, token permissions, test execution, artifacts and the fail-closed Provider Tests gate (769-789) are unchanged. docs/developer/build.md:228-251 documents that mapping and whole-lane allocation; its timestamp and unchanged file mode introduce no executable behavior.
No supported security regression was identified: these changes do not alter serving authorization, attestation, request encryption, cache scope or billing. Relevant concerns are adversarial provider-host execution and build/test integrity (TB-003, TB-007, T-013, T-034, T-054), plus resource availability. T-041 cache controls are not changed by the test environment settings shown in surrounding source. Sandbox routing already existed; this patch does not establish a new host-trust bypass or exposure of signing credentials.
Integration must verify the distinct-lane allocation contract in .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml, referenced at ci.yml:37: repeated macos_arm64 profiles should produce all five exact output keys, allocate isolated runner capacity without double-booking, and preserve validated labels and per-lane fallback on partial grants. That implementation is not supplied here, so documentation alone cannot establish the contract. This remains a material routing/integration uncertainty, not evidence of a vulnerability. Unchanged callers and dependencies were not audited.
